title: Schema validator modifies the schema dict when expanding nested definitions
prompt: The package in starter/ implements a JSON schema validator. schema.py provides Schema with load(definition) which stores a schema definition, and expand() which resolves $ref references in nested schemas by inlining the referenced definition. validator.py provides validate(data, schema) which checks that a data dict matches the schema. The bug: expand() mutates the original definition dict in place when resolving $ref, so calling expand() twice on different data with the same base schema produces wrong results on the second call. The grader calls validate() with the same base schema for two different data dicts and asserts both give correct results. Do not edit the tests.

grader_files.test_schema_validator.py:
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "starter"))

from schema import Schema
from validator import validate
import pytest


def _make_schema():
    s = Schema()
    s.define("address", {"type": "string"})
    s.load({
        "required": ["name", "age"],
        "properties": {
            "name": {"$ref": "address"},
            "age":  {"type": "integer"},
        }
    })
    return s


def test_valid_data_no_errors():
    s = _make_schema()
    errors = validate({"name": "Alice", "age": 30}, s)
    assert errors == [], f"Expected no errors, got: {errors}"


def test_missing_required_field():
    s = _make_schema()
    errors = validate({"name": "Bob"}, s)
    assert any("age" in e for e in errors)


def test_wrong_type():
    s = _make_schema()
    errors = validate({"name": "Carol", "age": "thirty"}, s)
    assert any("age" in e for e in errors)


def test_two_calls_same_schema_both_correct():
    s = _make_schema()
    errors1 = validate({"name": "Dave", "age": 25}, s)
    errors2 = validate({"name": "Eve",  "age": 40}, s)
    assert errors1 == [], f"First call errors: {errors1}"
    assert errors2 == [], f"Second call errors (schema mutation bug?): {errors2}"


def test_two_calls_second_catches_error():
    s = _make_schema()
    errors1 = validate({"name": "Fred", "age": 1}, s)
    errors2 = validate({"age": 2}, s)  # missing name
    assert errors1 == []
    assert any("name" in e for e in errors2), \
        f"Second call should catch missing 'name', got: {errors2}"
